Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 23, verse 1–7:

(p-4386) Surat al-Mu'minun

It is named "al-Mu'minun" (the Believers) because it includes the sublime attributes of the believers and their outcomes at its beginning and in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are, out of fear of their Lord, apprehensive﴾ up to His saying ﴿...who are foremost in good deeds﴾. This was noted by al-Mahayimi. It is a Meccan surah. Some scholars excepted from it one verse: ﴿Until, when We seize their affluent ones with punishment, they will cry out﴾ up to His saying ﴿...in despair﴾. Its number of verses is one hundred and eighteen.

Imam Ahmad, Muslim and others narrated from Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) led the dawn prayer in Makkah and began Surat al-Mu'minun. When he reached the mention of Musa and Harun, or the mention of Isa, a cough seized him and he bowed (in ruku')."

(p-4387) In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Commentary on His Exalted saying:

[1–7] ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾ ﴿who are during their prayer humbly submissive﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 2] ﴿and who turn away from ill speech﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 3] ﴿and who are observers of zakah﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 4] ﴿and who guard their private parts﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 5] ﴿except from their spouses or what their right hands possess, for indeed, they are not to be blamed﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 6] ﴿But whoever seeks beyond that, then it is those who are the transgressors﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 7].

﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾, i.e., they entered into the great triumph. ﴿Who are during their prayer humbly submissive﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 2], i.e., they are humble with fear and stillness of the limbs, because awe and dread have taken possession of their hearts. ﴿And who turn away from ill speech﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 3], i.e., from superfluity and what does not concern them of words and deeds, turning away throughout most of their times, being absorbed in seriousness.

﴿And who are observers of zakah﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 4], i.e., for purification from the vice of stinginess. It has been said: the surah is Meccan, and zakah was prescribed in Medina? The answer to this: what was prescribed in Medina was only the specific rates and amounts. Otherwise, the basic principle of giving in charity from surplus was legislated at the beginning of the mission, so there is no need to claim that the intended meaning is purification of souls from shirk and disobedience, since that is not what comes to mind first.

{﴿And who guard their private parts﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 5] ﴿except from their spouses or what their right hands possess, for indeed, they are not to be blamed﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 6]} because that is the permitted right (p-4388) ﴿But whoever seeks beyond that, then it is those who are the transgressors﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 7], i.e., the complete transgressors, who commit it against themselves.

Remarks:

The first: The verse indicates that the servant's success is conditioned upon guarding his private parts, and that there is no path to success without it. This verse contains three matters: whoever does not guard his private parts is not among the successful; he is among the blameworthy; and among the transgressors. Thus he loses success, deserves the name of transgression, and falls into blame. So enduring the pain of desire and its struggle is easier than some of that. Allah the Exalted commanded His Prophet to order the believers to lower their gaze and guard their private parts, and to teach them that He is witnessing their deeds, aware of them, knowing the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal. Since the origin of this is from the gaze, He placed the command to lower it before guarding the private parts, for incidents begin from looking, just as most of a fire begins from a small spark. Then it becomes a glance, then a passing thought, then a step, then a sin. The second: It is narrated from Imam Ahmad that he said: "I know of no sin after killing greater than fornication."

He argued with the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the greatest sin?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then what?" He said: "That you kill your child out of fear that he will share your food." I said: "Then what?" He said: "That you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbor." The Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned from each type its highest form, so that his answer would correspond to the questioner's question. (p-4389) For he was asked about the greatest sin, and he answered with what includes mention of the greatest of its types and what is greatest within each type. The greatest type of fornication is that one commits it with his neighbor's wife. For the corruption of fornication multiplies according to the multiplicity of the right it violates. Fornication with a woman who has a husband is greater in sin and punishment than fornication with one who has no husband, since it involves violating the husband's sanctity, corrupting his bed, attributing to him a lineage that is not his, and other forms of harm to him. So it is greater in sin and crime than fornication with a woman who is not married. If it happens that the woman is a close relative of his, severing her kinship is added to that.

[15–17] ﴿Then indeed, after that, you will surely die.﴾ ﴿Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, you will be raised up.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 16] ﴿And We have certainly created above you seven paths, and We have not been unaware of creation.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 17].

﴿Then indeed, after that﴾, i.e., after what has been mentioned of the marvelous matters and the attainment of these perfections: ﴿you will surely die﴾, i.e., you are certainly going to death.

Al-Mahayimi said: The Wise does not destroy what He has perfected through various kinds of perfecting, and therefore He will resurrect him, as He said: ﴿Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, you will be raised up﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 16], i.e., from your graves for reckoning and recompense. ﴿And We have certainly created above you seven paths﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 17], i.e., seven heavens, which are paths for the angels, and in which the stars move along their courses.

Some astronomers (in explaining this verse) said: i.e., seven orbits corresponding to the seven heavens; for each heaven there is a path along which move what is with it of moons. [18] ﴿And We sent down from the sky water in a measured amount, and We caused it to settle in the earth, and indeed, We are able to take it away.﴾

﴿And We sent down from the sky water in a measured amount﴾ i.e., with a measure by which they reach their benefit. Commentary of al-Qasimi (*Mahasin al-Ta'wil*) on Surah 23, verses 23–25:

When God, exalted is He, had explained the proofs of divine unity (*tawhid*), He followed them with accounts of the sending of the messengers, because of the exaltedness of His word. So He, glorified is He, said:

(p. 4395) Discussion of the interpretation (*ta'wil*) of His statement, exalted is He:

[23:23–25] ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he said, "O my people, worship God; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then be wary of God?" ﴾ ﴿So the eminent ones among his people who disbelieved said, "This is only a human being like yourselves who wants to make himself superior over you. And if God had willed, He would have sent down angels. We never heard of this among our forefathers of old."﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 24] ﴿"He is only a man possessed by madness, so wait for him for a time."﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 25].

﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he said, "O my people, worship God; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then be wary of God?"﴾ ﴿So the eminent ones among his people who disbelieved said, "This is only..."﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 24]: i.e., the one calling to the worship of God alone, by claiming the messengership from Himself: ﴿...only a human being like yourselves who wants to make himself superior over you﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 24]: i.e., who seeks to gain superiority over you and to lead you, like His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And that you two might have greatness in the land﴾ [Yunus: 78]. ﴿And if God had willed﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 24]: i.e., the sending of a messenger, ﴿He would have sent down angels﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 24]: i.e., from heaven. ﴿We never heard of this﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 24]: i.e., of anything like what he calls to. ﴿Among our forefathers of old﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 24]. ﴿"He is only a man possessed by madness, so wait for him for a time."﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 25]: i.e., perhaps he will return or recover from his madness, or he will persist, and then we will plot against him.

Al-Razi said: Know that He, glorified is He, did not mention the answer to these five doubts of theirs, because of their feebleness and the clear invalidity of them. This is because every intelligent person knows that a messenger does not become a messenger except because he is of the same kind as an angel. He becomes so only by being distinguished from others by miracles. So whether he is of the angelic kind or the human kind, when the miracle appears through him, he must be a messenger. Indeed, making the messenger one of mankind is better, for the reason explained earlier in the preceding surah, namely that kinship is the source of familiarity and intimacy. As for their saying: ﴿...wants to make himself superior over you﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 24] (p. 4396), if they meant by it his desire to show his superiority so that obedience to him becomes binding on them, then this is obligatory for the messenger. If they meant by it that he would rise above them through arrogance, tyranny and imposing submission, then the prophets are free of that. As for their saying: ﴿We never heard of this﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 24], it is an argument from the absence of precedent as proof of the non-existence of a thing, and it is extremely weak, because the absence of precedent does not prove the non-existence of the thing. How could the absence of precedent indicate its non-existence? As for their saying: ﴿He is possessed by madness﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 25], they lied, because they knew by necessity the perfection of his reason. As for their saying: ﴿So wait for him﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 25], it is weak, because if the proof of his prophethood appears, which is the miracle, it is obligatory for them to accept his word immediately, and it is not permissible to postpone that until his rule becomes established, because political success does not indicate the truth. And if the miracle does not appear, it is not permissible to accept his word, whether or not his rule appears. Since these answers are of the utmost clarity, God, glorified is He, therefore left them aside. End.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[31] ﴿Then We produced after them another generation.﴾

﴿Then We produced after them another generation.﴾ They are ʿĀd or Thamūd. Al-Shihāb said: There is nothing in the verse that specifies these people. However, the first view is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him and his father. And al-Kashf (al-Kashshāf) supported it by the fact that their story comes after the story of Noah in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, Hūd, and others. And most of the exegetes hold this view. As for those who held that they are Thamūd, the people of Ṣāliḥ, peace be upon him, they cited the mention of the Blast (al-Ṣayḥah), because they are the ones destroyed by it, as it is stated explicitly in this sūrah.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 23, verses 46–48:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[46–48] ﴿To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they waxed proud, for they were a haughty people.﴾ ﴿So they said, "Shall we believe two mortals like ourselves, while their people are servants to us?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 47] ﴿So they denied them, and became among those destroyed.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 48].

(p-4401) ﴿To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they waxed proud﴾ meaning: they refused submission and refused to send the Children of Israel with Musa to the land of Canaan, and to free them from that servitude imposed on them. ﴿For they were a haughty people﴾ meaning: rebellious. ﴿So they said, "Shall we believe two mortals like ourselves, while their people are servants to us?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 47] ﴿So they denied them, and became among those destroyed.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 48] meaning: those drowned in the sea.

Benefit:

Al-Zamakhshari said: "Bashar (mortal, human) may be singular or plural: ﴿a human being, well-proportioned﴾ [Maryam: 17]; ﴿two mortals﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 47]; ﴿if you see any mortal﴾ [Maryam: 26]. And mithl (like) and ghayr (other) are described by both the dual, the plural, the masculine and the feminine: ﴿indeed, you would then be like them﴾ [al-Nisa': 140]; ﴿and of the earth the like of them﴾ [al-Talaq: 12]. It is also said: 'they are two like him' and 'they are his likes': ﴿Indeed, those you call upon besides Allah are servants like you﴾ [al-A'raf: 194]."

The commentary on His saying, exalted is He:

[49–50] ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, that they might be guided﴾ ﴿And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign, and We sheltered them on a high ground, a place of stability and running water﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 50].

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾, i.e., the Torah. ﴿That they might be guided﴾, i.e., his people, ﴿that they might be guided﴾, i.e., to the path of truth, by means of what it contains of laws (shara'i') and rulings (ahkam). ﴿And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 50], i.e., a proof of Our overwhelming power, because she bore him without any touching (masis). So "sign" is one matter attributed to both of them. Or the meaning is: We made the son of Mary a sign by the extraordinary things (khariq) that appeared from him, and his mother a sign in that she bore him without touching, and the first was omitted because the second indicates it. ﴿And We sheltered them﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 50], i.e., We made their refuge, i.e., their dwelling, ﴿on a high ground﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 50], i.e., elevated land, ﴿a place of stability﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 50], i.e., a settled place of level, even land. It is related from Qatadah: "possessing fruits (thimar) and water," meaning that the inhabitants settle there because of the fruits. ﴿And running water﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 50], i.e., and apparent flowing water, from (ma'ana al-ma' idha jara, "the water flowed"), or perceptible by the eye (min 'anahu, "when he perceived it with his eye").

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 23, verse 51:

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[51] ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds. Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do.﴾

﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds. Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do.﴾ This is an address and a direct speech to all the prophets, according to the time and era of each one. Thus Jesus is included in it by way of primary inclusion. Or it may be the beginning of a statement, mentioned as an alert that the provision of the means of comfort was not specific to him, and that the permissibility of good things for the prophets is an ancient law, and as an argument against the monks (al-rahabina) in their rejection of good things. His words, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, mean: a righteous deed, for it is the means by which the happiness of both abodes is attained. His words, ﴿Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do﴾, mean: He is One of knowledge, nothing of it is hidden from Me. So I will reward you for all of it, and pay you your wages and your reward for it, so take up the righteous deeds and strive.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[52] ﴿And indeed this, your community, is one community, and I am your Lord, so fear Me.﴾

﴿And indeed this, your community﴾ means: know that this is your religion and your sacred law which you follow, ﴿one community﴾, that is, one religion (millah), and it is the sacred law of Islam: the submission of the face to Allah, exalted is He, by worshipping Him alone. Caution (tanbih):

Imam Abu Muslim al-Isfahani went astray in what al-Razi transmitted from him, holding that His saying ﴿But their hearts are in confusion about this﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 63] up to the end of the verse is a continuation of the attributes of the fearful believers. As if He, glorified is He, said after describing them: ﴿And We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity﴾, and its conclusion is what these fearful ones brought, ﴿And with Us is a Book which preserves their deeds, speaking with truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾ Rather, We fully reward them for all their deeds. ﴿But their hearts are in confusion about this﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 63] is also a description of them as being bewildered, as if He said: And they, along with that fear and dread, are like those bewildered about whether their deeds are accepted or rejected. ﴿And they have deeds other than that﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 63], that is, they also have supererogatory acts and forms of righteousness beyond what they are upon, either deeds they have already done in the past or those they will do in the future. Then He, exalted is He, returned.

Al-Razi said: Abu Muslim's view is better, because when it is possible to refer the speech to what is connected to it, namely the mention of the fearful ones, it is better than referring it to what is distant from it. A person may be described, due to the intensity of his thought about the matter of his afterlife, as having his heart in confusion, meaning that thought has taken hold of him regarding whether his deed is accepted or rejected, and whether he has performed it as it should be or fallen short. End of quotation.

Furthermore, the structure of the noble verse permits this. However, the attribute of being in confusion (ghamrah) is not at all ascribed to the believers; rather, it is ascribed only to the hearts of the criminals, as you see in the verses before. Sound taste and attention to the parallel verses reject, most strongly, what Abu Muslim has put forward. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 23, verses 65–67:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[65–67] ﴿Do not cry out for help today; indeed, you will not be helped by Us.﴾ ﴿My verses were recited to you, but you turned back on your heels,﴾ ﴿being arrogant about it, conversing by night, speaking abusively.﴾

﴿Do not cry out for help today﴾: meaning, it is said to them as a rebuke: "Do not cry out, for crying out will not benefit you." ﴿Indeed, you will not be helped by Us.﴾ ﴿My verses were recited to you, but you turned back on your heels﴾: meaning, you turned away from hearing them with the utmost aversion. ﴿Being arrogant about it﴾: meaning, about the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Haram). The reference was made implicit (by the pronoun) because of their well-known arrogance concerning it, and because they had no source of pride except that they were its custodians. It has also been permitted to take (mustakbirin) as implying the meaning of (mukadhdhibin, denying), with the pronoun referring to the Noble Revelation (al-Tanzil al-Karim); that is, denying it with the denial of arrogance. They did not mention the possibility of the pronoun referring to "turning back" (al-nukus), as an indication of the increase in their obstinacy, and that they boast of this aversion and do not fear what they are warned of, like His words: ﴿He turned away arrogantly﴾ [Luqman: 7]. And it is not far-fetched, so reflect. ﴿Conversing by night, speaking abusively﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 67]: meaning, they hold nocturnal gatherings (yasmurun) mentioning the Qur'an and disparaging it, calling it sorcery, poetry, and the like. This is the meaning of (tahjurun) from al-hujr (with a damma), which is obscene speech. Or its meaning is "you turn away," from al-hajr (with a fatha).

Note:

Abu al-Baqa' said: (samiran) is also a circumstantial accusative (hal), and it is a verbal noun (masdar), like their saying (qum qa'iman, stand standing). Some verbal nouns have come in the form of the active participle, such as al-'aqibah and al-'afiyah. It has also been said: it is singular in the place of the plural, meaning it is a singular placed in the position of the plural. End of quote.

Thus it is a singular used in place of the plural. It has also been said that it is a collective noun (ism jam'), like hajj, hadir, rakib, and ghaib. Al-Shihab said: On the reading that it is a verbal noun, it also covers both few and many, by consideration of its root. However, the occurrence of a verbal noun on the pattern (fa'il) is rare. It has also been read as (sumaran) with a damma and shadda, and as (summar) with an added alif.

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[68] ﴿Have they not pondered the Word, or has there come to them what did not come to their forefathers of old?﴾

﴿Have they not pondered the Word﴾, that is, the Qur'an, so that they would know that it is the manifest truth, and thus believe in it and in the one who brought it. ﴿Or has there come to them what did not come to their forefathers of old﴾, that is, of guidance and truth. So they deemed it an innovation and found it strange, and thus they fell into the disbelief and misguidance into which they fell. Yet the coming of what is unfamiliar does not necessitate aversion, because what is familiar may well be falsehood, and wisdom therefore requires warning against it.

The commentary on the Lord's words:

[69–70] ﴿Or do they not recognize their Messenger, so that they deny him?﴾ ﴿Or do they say, "There is madness in him"? Rather, he has brought them the truth, but most of them are averse to the truth.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 70]

﴿Or do they not recognize their Messenger, so that they deny him?﴾ That is: they reject what he was sent with. This is another rebuke, pointing to the greatness of their ignorance, in that they did not know his station, nor did they comprehend the secret of what he was sent with, which is regrettable. As He said: ﴿Alas for the servants! No messenger comes to them but they mock him.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 30]

﴿Or do they say, "There is madness in him"?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 70] That is: madness (junun), or jinn who have seized him. This is another rebuke, containing a wonder at the variety of their denial and the ingenuity of their obstinacy. Then He indicated that what led them to this was nothing but their refusal to accept the truth out of arrogance and insolence, by His words: ﴿Rather, he has brought them the truth, but most of them are averse to the truth.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 70] That is: because of the deviation and perversion within them.

(p-4409) Al-Qashani said: When they nullified their capacities and extinguished their light with rust (rayn) and sealing (tab'), in accordance with the demands of the soul's faculties and natural disposition, and their veiling by dark coverings from the light of guidance and intellect became intense, they were unable to reflect upon the Word, nor did they understand the realities of monotheism and justice. So they attributed him to jinn-possession and did not recognize him, owing to the opposition between light and darkness and the contrariety between falsehood and truth; and they denied him and hated the truth that he brought.

Those who veil themselves from the world of light with darkness, and from holiness with defilement, are only immersed in wrongdoing, hatred and enmity, and in leaning toward multiplicity. So they are undoubtedly deviating from the path, veering off toward its opposite. He is in one valley and they are in another.

Al-Zamakhshari said: In these verses He has laid the proof upon them, cut off their excuses, and given their reasons. The one who was sent to them is a man whose affair and condition are well known, whose secret and public conduct are known, deserving that someone like him be chosen for the message from among them. He did not come forward to claim such a great claim falsely, nor did he make it a ladder to gain from their worldly goods or to seek their wealth. He called them only to the religion of Islam, which is the straight path, while exposing what lay hidden of their ailments: their neglect of reflection and contemplation, their recklessness in abandoning the religion of their misguided fathers without proof, and their pretext that he is a madman, after the truth had become manifest and the confirmation from God through miracles and clear signs had been established, and their aversion to the truth and their turning away from what holds their share of the reminder. And His saying, exalted is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[75] ﴿Even if We had mercy on them and removed the harm that is upon them, they would persist in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾

﴿Even if We had mercy on them and removed the harm that is upon them, they would persist in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾

Ibn Jarir said: That is: Even if We had mercy on these who do not believe in the Hereafter, and lifted from them the famine and dearth they suffer, and the harm of hunger and emaciation: ﴿they would persist in their transgression﴾, meaning in their obstinacy and their boldness against their Lord; ﴿wandering blindly﴾, meaning hesitating and wavering.

Ibn Kathir pointed to another meaning, saying: He, exalted is He, informs of their severe hardness in their disbelief, that if He removed the harm from them and made them understand the Qur'an, they would not submit to it, but would persist in their disbelief, their obstinacy and their transgression, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. **The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

﴿And We had certainly seized them with punishment, yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they supplicate.﴾

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: That is, We had certainly seized these polytheists with Our punishment, sent down upon them Our might and Our wrath, constricted their livelihoods, made their lands barren, and killed their chiefs by the sword, yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord, that is, they did not submit to Him so as to obey His command and prohibition, or turn back to His obedience. **The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:**

[77] ﴿Until, when We open upon them a gate of severe punishment, behold, they will be in despair therein.﴾

﴿Until, when We open upon them a gate of severe punishment﴾ means what befell them of fighting and killing on the day of Badr, or the gate of famine and hardship. The latter is what was narrated from Mujahid (Mujahid ibn Jabr) and what Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) preferred. ﴿Behold, they will be in despair therein﴾ means: sorrowful and regretful over what had passed from them in denying the signs of God, at a time when regret and sorrow will not benefit them. The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[78] ﴿It is He who brought into being for you hearing, sight and hearts; little is it that you give thanks.﴾

﴿It is He who brought into being for you hearing, sight and hearts﴾, that is, so that you might hear, see and understand. ﴿Little is it that you give thanks﴾, that is, for God's blessing in that, by employing them for what they were created for. And it means: to perceive.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 23, verse 88–89:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[88–89] ﴿Say: "In whose hand is the dominion of all things, who gives protection while none can be protected against Him, if you know?" They will say, "[It belongs] to Allah." Say, "Then how are you deluded?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 88–89].

﴿Say: "In whose hand is the dominion of all things, who gives protection"﴾ meaning: He rescues whomever He wills from one who intends him harm. ﴿while none can be protected against Him﴾ meaning: no one can prevent Him from one whom He intends harm, so as to repel from him His punishment and His retribution. ﴿if you know?﴾ ﴿They will say, "[It belongs] to Allah." Say, "Then how are you deluded?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 89], meaning: you are deceived away from His oneness and obedience to Him, despite the matter being manifest and the proofs being abundant. Thus "magic" (sihr) is used figuratively for deception. The repetition of ﴿if you know﴾ is for their contempt and for declaring them ignorant, given the complete clarity of the matter.

In (al-Iklil), Makki said: In these verses there is evidence for the permissibility of disputing with disbelievers and falsifiers, establishing the proof and manifesting the falsehood of their statements and doctrines, and the obligation to consider the arguments of one who opposes the religion of Allah.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[101] ﴿Then when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask about one another.﴾

﴿Then when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship between them that Day﴾ That is: because of the severity of the terror, from the onslaught of what occupies the mind, so that compassion and mutual affection vanish through it, since: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother﴾ [Abasa: 34] ﴿and his mother and his father﴾ [Abasa: 35] ﴿and his spouse and his children﴾ [Abasa: 36] ﴿For every one of them that Day, there will be a matter that preoccupies him﴾ [Abasa: 37]. And the negation of the benefit of lineage when such a thing overtakes people is well known, as one has said:

"There is no lineage today, nor any friendship; the tear has widened beyond the patch."

﴿And nor will they ask about one another﴾ That is: none of them will question another, because of the greatness of the dread, the severity of the terrors they are in, and their distraction from what was between them of conditions. Thus the bonds and connections that existed between them are severed. It is clear that the negation of questioning applies only at the time of the blowing, as indicated by His saying: ﴿Then﴾, that is, at the time of rising from the graves and the terror of the place of standing, each one is occupied with himself. As for what comes after that, questioning may occur, as God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And some of them will turn to others, questioning one another﴾ [al-Saffat: 27], because the Day of Resurrection is a long day, containing stations and positions. So questioning may occur in some of them, and in others there is a bewilderment that prevents it.

Note:

Some exegetes have related here reports about the benefit of the Prophetic lineage. It would have been excellent if some of them had been narrated in the two Sahihs, or in the musnads of those who committed themselves to authenticity.

The Commentary on the Interpretation of His Saying, may He be exalted:

[102–104] ﴿Then whoever's scales are heavy, those are the successful.﴾ ﴿And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost their souls; in Hell they will abide eternally.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 103] ﴿The Fire will scorch their faces, and they therein will be grimacing.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 104].

﴿Then whoever's scales are heavy﴾, i.e., whose good deeds outweigh: ﴿those are the successful﴾. ﴿And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost their souls﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 103], i.e., by squandering what they were granted of the capacity (al-isti'dad) to profit in the trade of perfection, through the innate nature of faith (fitrat al-iman) and righteous deeds. The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[111–114] ﴿Indeed, I have rewarded them today for what they endured; indeed, they are the triumphant.﴾ ﴿He said, "How many years did you remain on the earth?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 112] ﴿They said, "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who count."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 113] ﴿He said, "You remained only a little, if only you had known."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 114].

﴿Indeed, I have rewarded them today for what they endured; indeed, they are the triumphant.﴾ ﴿He said﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 112], i.e., Allah, or the angel commanded to question them: ﴿How many years did you remain on the earth?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 112] ﴿They said, "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who count."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 113] ﴿He said, "You remained only a little, if only you had known."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 114], i.e., a little, some amount. Or, "if you had been among the people of knowledge." The answer (al-jawab) is omitted, relying on the indication of what preceded it. That is: "You would have known on that day the brevity of your stay in it, as you know it today, and you would have acted according to its requirement, and you would not have clung to it."

Al-Razi said: The purpose of this question is rebuke and reproach. They used to deny any stay in the Hereafter at all, and did not count any stay except in the abode of this world. They thought that after death annihilation endures, with no return. When they were in the Fire and were certain that it is everlasting, and that they would abide in it forever, He asked them, "How many years did you remain on the earth?" as a reminder to them that what they had supposed to be a long enduring is, compared with what they denied, a small thing. Thereupon they would feel (p-٤٤٢١) regret for what they had believed in the world, since they now were certain of its opposite. So the purpose is not merely the question, but what has been mentioned.

Al-Zamakhshari said: They considered the period of their stay in the world to be short, in comparison with their eternal abiding and with what they were suffering in the Fire. For the one who is tested feels the days of his trial to be long, and considers short the days of ease that passed before it. Or, because they were in happiness, and the days of happiness are short. Or, because what has passed is as though it had never been. Allah confirmed their estimation of the years of their stay in the world, and rebuked them for the heedlessness in which they had been. It is read: ﴿فَسَلِ العادِّينَ﴾ ("so ask those who count," with the verb read as fasali, without the alif of the imperative, the reading of some reciters), and the meaning is: We do not know the number of those years, except that we consider it little and reckon it a day or part of a day, because of what we are in of punishment, and it is not in us to count them. So ask whoever is able to count, and whose thought is capable of reaching it. It was said: ask the angels who count the lifespans of the servants and enumerate their deeds. End of quotation.

[115-118] ﴿Did you think that We had created you in vain, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ ﴿Exalted is Allah, the True King; there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne.﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 116] ﴿And whoever invokes along with Allah another deity, for which he has no proof, then his account is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 117] ﴿And say, "My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful."﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 118].

﴿Did you think that We had created you in vain﴾, meaning without wisdom, so that you denied the resurrection. ﴿And that you would not be returned to Us﴾, meaning for recompense. ﴿Exalted is Allah﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 116], meaning He is far above what you describe, because He is ﴿the True King﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 116], meaning the One who alone disposes affairs, who intended by creation that He be known and worshipped. He does not leave recompense unfulfilled, but establishes the truth: ﴿there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 116], meaning the Great, the Glorious. It is also read with the nominative case: ﴿And whoever invokes along with Allah another deity, for which he has no proof﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 117]. (p-4422) Ibn Jarir said: "Whoever invokes along with the One to Whom worship alone is fitting another object of worship, for which he has no argument or evidence regarding what he claims, then the reckoning of his evil deed is with his Lord, who will repay him for it when he comes before Him.
